common_name: Oriental Gold Itoh Peony (Golden-Yellow Semi-Double Intersectional Peony with Strawberry-Red Flares)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in early fall so roots establish before winter; set the eyes no more than 1-2 inches below the soil surface.

directions: Oriental Gold is one of the earliest Itoh intersectional peonies grown outside Japan, hybridized in the late 1940s or 1950s and brought to the United States in the early 1970s by importer Louis Smirnow, predating the wave of American-bred Itoh cultivars that followed decades later. Its golden-yellow, semi-double flowers carry strawberry-red flares at the petal bases and a light lemony fragrance, opening late in the season on a dense, upright-and-spreading plant. Grow in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, giving afternoon shade in hot climates, and leave the clump undisturbed for several seasons since Itoh peonies take time to reach full bloom size. Like other intersectional hybrids it dies back to the ground each winter rather than persisting as a woody shrub.
